newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler cuts Q2 output plan by 99,700 units.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler cuts Q2 output plan by 99,700 units.

text.p: Chrysler Corp said Thursday it reduced its second quarter worldwide production schedule by 99,700 vehicles as a result of a month-long engine plant strike that forced it to halt much of its light truck production.
Chrysler said its latest second quarter schedule calls for production of 718,500 cars and trucks worldwide, down from an estimated 818,200 vehicles in a schedule released a month ago.
Chrysler said it now plans to build 473,500 trucks during the second quarter at plants in the United States, Canada, Mexico and Austria.
A month ago, Chrysler had scheduled production of 570,200 trucks during the second quarter.
Chrysler also said it reduced second quarter passenger car production by 3,000 units compared with a month ago to 245,000.

On Tuesday, Chrysler said production losses due to the strike would reduce its second quarter net income by about $450 million, or $0.65 a share. The strike at Chrysler's Mound Road Engine Plant in Detroit forced it to halt production of Dodge Ram and Dakota pickup trucks, large vans and Jeep Grand Cherokee sport/utility vehicles.
